_comment: What the farm canary claims to prove, keyed by the names its checks carry
in @pytest.mark.capability(...). The report renders one row per entry --
validated, failed, blocked, skipped, or NOT VALIDATED when no check in the
Every entry here is about hardware the farm owns: an ESP, a cable, a hub,
the rig's access point, its broker, its uplink. None of it is about
painlessMesh or about any consumer's firmware, which is the point -- a red
canary must never be read as somebody's regression.
Each check runs once per board, so a capability that failed names the
boards it failed on: red on every board is the farm, red on one is that
esp.boot: Every board starts, answers, and reports its silicon, heap, flash and reset reason
esp.serial: Every board returns a kilobyte-long line byte for byte over its console
esp.flash: Every board writes a key to NVS (LittleFS on the ESP8266), reads it back, and erases it
esp.reset: The rig restarts every board over its reset lines, proven by a new boot id
esp.radio.scan: Every board's receiver sees the rig access point, with a plausible RSSI
esp.radio.join: Every board associates with the rig access point and is given a DHCP lease
farm.uplink: The rig's gateway probe answers every board over the rig network
farm.queue: The rig's MQTT broker accepts a message published by every board
